title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board; directors and company secretary of any subsidiary; any person entitled to receive equity performance rights and/or options under an equity incentive scheme of the Company; Executives (persons, whether or not Directors, involved in strategic or operational management, including the Company Secretary and relevant service providers); and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: A Restricted Person's immediate family (including a spouse or equivalent, or dependent), family company or trust. Each Restricted Person is personally responsible for ensuring their Associated Parties comply with the same restrictions.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Subset of Restricted Persons (the Board) distinguished for the duty to notify ASX of shareholding changes under Listing Rule 3.19A and to enter a Director disclosure agreement under Guidance Note 22, and for the 'bona fide gifts to a Director' exclusion.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate further periods of time as a prohibited period, and the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their Associated Parties trading at any time. Confidentiality of these ad hoc periods or embargoes is not addressed.

rules.detail: Not named directly; the Securities definition (interests in shares, options or debentures, and managed investment scheme interests, as defined in the Corporations Act) does not itself extend to third-party derivatives. However, any derivative that operates to limit the economic risk of holding Company securities — which a collar inherently does — is caught by the standalone Hedging prohibition and is banned outright, with no clearance route or vesting-state carve-out.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights). Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban applying to shares, options and rights alike, with no clearance mechanism, exceptional-circumstances gateway, or vesting-state distinction stated anywhere in the Policy.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).

rules.detail: Not named. A monetisation instrument that caps upside or otherwise limits economic risk on the holding is a 'financial product that operates to limit economic risk' and so falls within the absolute hedging ban.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

Including Company securities in a margin loan portfolio, entering a margin lending arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, or selling to satisfy a margin call are all permitted only with the Company's prior consent, which may be made conditional (e.g. on the circumstances in which securities may be sold to satisfy a call).
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: Entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities (i.e. granting security over them) is expressly listed as requiring the Company's prior consent.
rules.evidence: Such dealing would include: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of securities in the Company; transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account; and selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.

rules.detail: Clause 1.11 is framed specifically around 'margin loans'/'margin lending arrangements'; it does not use the broader 'any secured financing arrangement' language seen in some other issuers' policies, so whether a bespoke bank facility secured over the shares but not structured as a margin loan needs the same consent is not entirely clear on the wording, though the same consent should be sought given the clause's evident purpose.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: No holding period or intention-based short-term trading restriction is stated.

clearance.approver: Chairperson (or another Director where the Chairperson is involved), in conference with the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities ... prior to such intended dealings. The Company Secretary will confer with the Chairperson in relation to any proposed dealing. ... Where, in exceptional circumstances, and it is the only reasonable course of action available to a Restricted Person ... clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.

The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this Clause 1.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 5 business days after any change in relevant interest
clearance.evidence: In accordance with Listing Rule 3.19A, a Director of a Company must notify ASX within 5 business days after any change in his or her relevant interest in the Company's securities.

exemption_authority: The Chairperson (or another Director where the Chairperson is involved) may grant clearance to sell, but not purchase, during a prohibited period only in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement, or other circumstances the Chairperson deems exceptional), and may not do so while inside information exists. The Company separately holds a consent power over margin lending arrangements (1.11), and the Board has an absolute, unqualified discretion to embargo trading at any time (1.5).

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights). Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar is precisely a transaction in financial products (a purchased put and written call) that limits the economic risk of holding the shares, so it is banned outright for every Restricted Person, with no clearance mechanism, vesting-state carve-out, or exceptional-circumstances gateway available at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike hedging, financing secured against the shares is not banned outright but merely requires the Company's prior (potentially conditional) consent; however, the clause is framed narrowly around 'margin loans' and it is unclear whether a bespoke bank facility not styled as a margin loan needs the same consent, though seeking it is the prudent course.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even genuine hardship or a court order can only ever authorise a sale during a prohibited period, never a purchase, which is relevant to how any collar unwind or settlement mechanics are structured if they fall inside a prohibited period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This unconditional, open-ended embargo power (separate from the fixed 5-business-day dividend/capital-management blackout) means the timing of a collar's entry, roll or unwind could be blocked without stated reason or notice.

summary: A funded collar with a bank is not achievable under this policy. Clause 1.10 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on Restricted Persons entering into any 'hedging arrangement', defined to include any transaction in a financial product that operates to limit the economic risk of holding Company securities — squarely covering a purchased put and written call — with no clearance mechanism, vesting-state carve-out, or exceptional-circumstances gateway available, unlike the general dealing and margin-loan regimes. The loan leg is treated differently: including WAM shares in a margin loan portfolio, entering a margin lending arrangement, transferring shares into a margin loan account, or selling to satisfy a margin call are all expressly permitted subject to the Company's prior, potentially conditional, consent, though this consent regime is framed narrowly around 'margin loans' rather than secured financing generally. Even setting the hedging ban aside, any dealing in WAM's shares needs advance written notice to the Company Secretary (who confers with the Chairperson), is barred within 5 business days of a dividend or material capital-management announcement or during any period the Board designates or embargoes at its absolute discretion, and during a prohibited period can only be cleared to sell (never to purchase) in genuine hardship, court-order, or other exceptional circumstances. Given the standalone and unqualified hedging prohibition, a bank-written collar cannot be entered by any Restricted Person regardless of vesting status or approval sought.
